items.title: Rent crisis forces over half of Spaniards to move or share
items.body: Rental prices hit a record €15.1/m² in May, forcing 53.7% of citizens to take action like moving to cheaper homes, sharing flats, or moving to suburbs. Meanwhile, 66% of households now spend over 30% of income on rent.

items.title: ECB expected to raise rates for first time in three years
items.body: The ECB is expected to raise its benchmark rate to 2.25% this week, the first hike since 2023. Pimco and Vanguard predict two more increases by year-end and another in early 2027, as inflation reached 3.2% in May.

items.title: Union demands €1,500 minimum net salary for all state employees
items.body: CCOO demands that no state employee earn less than €1,500 net per month, as 15% of the workforce earns near the SMI (minimum wage) of €1,221 in 14 payments. The union says rising costs are causing job offer rejections in expensive cities.

items.title: Former Sepi chief and PSOE official in public company scandal
items.body: Between 2019 and 2022, Vicente Martínez and Leire Díez allegedly pressured executives of state-owned companies for business opportunities under the political cover of ex-Vice President María Jesús Montero. Some deals went through while others were aborted, according to El Mundo.

items.title: US bombs Iran in retaliation for Apache helicopter downing
items.body: The US launched airstrikes on Iran in retaliation for the downing of an Apache helicopter. Iran responded by attacking US bases in Kuwait, Jordan, and radar installations in Bahrain.

items.title: Tax agency staff strike during Renta campaign over conditions
items.body: Tax agency (AEAT) employees held a 24-hour strike during the Renta (income tax) campaign, citing breaches of labor agreements. The agency said citizen services were not affected, according to Heraldo.

items.title: Spain to phase out paper medication vouchers in pharmacies
items.body: The Ministry of Health approved a decree to replace paper cupón precinto (seal voucher) with a digital verification system. Minister Mónica García said it ends 'the cutter, stickers, and bureaucracy' in pharmacies.
